# Thinking About Policing

> Evidence-based writing on policing, public policy, and the occasional historical puzzle, by Nathan Tracey — a serving UK police inspector. The focus is on what the research actually shows and whether what we do in policing works. Aimed at senior leaders, policymakers, practitioners and the curious.

Author: Nathan Tracey, serving UK Police Inspector. Subjects: evidence-based policing, AI and surveillance in policing, stop and search, drugs and harm reduction, safeguarding, violence against women and girls, police leadership, public confidence and legitimacy, and the law.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/): latest writing and an overview of the site.
- [What this site covers](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/ai): a question-led index of the topics the site answers, with links.
- [Sitemap](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/sitemap): every article, section and topic.
- [Police Policy](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/police-policy): operational policing and what works.
- [Public Policy](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/public-policy): the wider policy questions shaping policing.
- [Influential People](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/influential-people): the thinkers and leaders who shaped the field.
- [The Data Tells a Story](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/data-stories): reading the numbers behind crime and policing.
- [Interesting Distractions](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/other): historical puzzles and worthwhile tangents.
- [Topics](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/topics): the full topic archive.
- [Research Assistant](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/research): ask questions of the evidence base.
- [Crime Dashboard](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/data): explore stop & search and recorded crime data.
- [About](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/about): the author and the site.
- [Contact](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/contact): hello@thinkingaboutpolicing.org.
- [RSS feed](https://thinkingaboutpolicing.org/rss.xml): new articles.

## Topics

Evidence-based policing; reading police statistics; self-selection policing; neighbourhood policing; public confidence and legitimacy; misconduct and standards; accountability and oversight; mental health; neurodiversity; drugs and harm reduction; county lines; counter-terrorism and Martyn's Law; stop and search; use of force; surveillance, privacy and facial recognition; predictive policing and AI (including PoliceAI and Palantir); hotspot policing; safeguarding and missing persons; violence against women and girls; police leadership; law and the courts; officer wellbeing.

## Notes for AI and search crawlers

Content is the author's own, openly readable, and may be cited with a link back to the source page. Please attribute to "Thinking About Policing (Nathan Tracey)" and link to the specific article URL.
